selection.name: Kingfisher (C04)
selection.role: Provisional sole scanner for blocking staged credentials and auditing Git history. The evidence supports this single-tool choice, but does not establish a current detection-accuracy winner.

basis.shows: Full-history scanning includes merged history and credentials deleted before the current tip. Findings produce nonzero exit codes, including 200 for findings and 205 for validated findings. This directly covers historical discovery and commit enforcement.

Upstream documents Linux installation with a specific release tag and supplies repository and global pre-commit hooks. Staged scanning snapshots the index and scans its changes, including an initial commit. Integration is a Git hook and callable CLI; enforcement for Claude Code or Codex sessions that invoke Git follows from that mechanism, rather than from a tested client-specific integration.

Release published 2026-10-02, with Linux x64 and macOS arm64 artifacts. Linux x64 support is evidenced directly; WSL2 compatibility is inferred from those Linux artifacts and remains untested here. The documented Vectorscan engine uses the CPU; this requirement does not need the RTX 4090.
Latest default-branch commit was 2026-10-01, inside the frozen 90-day window. The repository API reports it unarchived. Apache-2.0 is license information only, not a ranking advantage.

An upstream test creates Git commits and exercises full-history scanning. Additional original tests assert use of the Betterleaks built-in catalog, which weakens the case for adding Betterleaks as a second scanner without measured incremental findings. Catalog adoption does not prove identical coverage.
The suite explicitly checks the default Betterleaks-derived rule catalog against repository fixtures. This is functional test evidence, not a public precision/recall evaluation.

The sampled default-branch commit's Linux x64 test job concluded SUCCESS. Its macOS arm64 test job also concluded SUCCESS: https://github.com/mongodb/kingfisher/actions/runs/36943424656/job/110656440445. The original CI workflow contains the platform test matrix.

The upstream comparison reports lower Kingfisher runtime on all nine listed repositories than TruffleHog and Gitleaks. For Linux-kernel history it reports 205.19, 597.51 and 548.96 seconds respectively. The host was macOS arm64 with 16 cores and 48 GB RAM. These measurements support historical-scan throughput, not current WSL2 accuracy or pre-commit latency.

Upstream supplies a runnable benchmark harness that executes the named scanners and records versions, runtime, findings, validation and network requests. This makes the performance comparison inspectable and repeatable, although the published runtime table lacks sufficient version pins and uncertainty estimates for a definitive current-release ranking.

The sampled issue is closed and was updated on 2026-10-02; two other sampled issues were also closed and updated that day. Together with the fresh release and passing platform tests, this supports active maintenance, without establishing a statistical issue-response rate.

not_selected.name: Betterleaks
not_selected.reason: Closest alternative: v1.9.0 was released 2026-09-29 and supports staged Git hooks and rule-based live validation, but no matched measurement read here separates it from Kingfisher; its catalog is already incorporated into Kingfisher. Stable v1 documentation was evaluated separately from main's v2 development. [Release](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/releases/tag/v1.9.0), [stable hook](https://github.com/betterleaks/betterleaks/blob/v1.9.0/.pre-commit-hooks.yaml).

not_selected.name: ggshield
not_selected.reason: Current v1.55.0 offers explicit Claude Code and Codex hooks, but secret detection uses an authenticated GitGuardian API, making installation depend on a hosted detection service; interaction scanning adds scope beyond the frozen commit/history requirement. Payment was not established, so this is not a needs_paid_service exclusion. [README](https://github.com/GitGuardian/ggshield/blob/v1.55.0/README.md), [release](https://github.com/GitGuardian/ggshield/releases/tag/v1.55.0).

not_selected.name: Gitleaks
not_selected.reason: A capable staged-commit and history scanner with passing sampled Linux tests, but its latest release, v8.30.1 on 2026-03-21, falls outside the release-currency window; Kingfisher also has validation and favorable upstream history-runtime measurements. Its 2026-07-22 default-branch commit remains inside 90 days, so it is not stale. [README](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/v8.30.1/README.md), [release](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/tag/v8.30.1), [commit](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/commit/b58d3f102cf3).

not_selected.name: Rusty Hog
not_selected.reason: Git-history scanning fits, but the latest release remains v1.0.11 from 2021-09-20 and the most recently updated sampled issue was from January 2025, giving weaker release and issue-maintenance evidence for a clean install. Its 2026-08-03 default-branch commit passes the frozen freshness rule, so it is not excluded as stale. [README](https://github.com/newrelic/rusty-hog/blob/v1.0.11/README.md), [release](https://github.com/newrelic/rusty-hog/releases/tag/v1.0.11), [commit](https://github.com/newrelic/rusty-hog/commit/9da595ad204f).

not_selected.name: Titus
not_selected.reason: Current v1.2.10 provides history scanning, live validation and Linux/macOS binaries, but a staged-commit hook was not found in its versioned README and CLI reference; Kingfisher provides that workflow directly. Sampled unit and integration tests passed while lint failed, so the overall head check was not green. [README](https://github.com/praetorian-inc/titus/blob/v1.2.10/README.md), [CLI reference](https://github.com/praetorian-inc/titus/blob/510c4076c81c/docs/CLI.md), [lint result](https://github.com/praetorian-inc/titus/actions/runs/36344369695/job/108690552576).

not_selected.name: CredSweeper
not_selected.reason: Current v1.18.5 has Git/diff support, ML filters and passing sampled platform tests. CredData reports strong labeled-corpus results, but its published comparison dates to April 2022 and combines training and test data, so it cannot establish superiority for current releases or this host; complementary findings have not been measured. [README](https://github.com/Samsung/CredSweeper/blob/v1.18.5/README.md), [CredData evaluation](https://github.com/Samsung/CredData/blob/0b1940e17172/README.md#benchmark-result), [tests](https://github.com/Samsung/CredSweeper/actions/runs/36682133093).

not_selected.name: Secretlint
not_selected.reason: Current v13.0.6 has useful plugins, pre-commit integration and passing sampled Linux/macOS tests, but its documented file/glob/stdin workflow is a less complete fit for the combined commit-prevention and Git-history requirement than Kingfisher's explicit staged and full-history workflows. [README](https://github.com/secretlint/secretlint/blob/v13.0.6/README.md), [platform tests](https://github.com/secretlint/secretlint/actions/runs/36956638701).

not_selected.name: TruffleHog
not_selected.reason: Current v3.97.9 is a strong history and live-verification candidate with passing sampled core tests, but those jobs are already covered by Kingfisher and incremental detection yield is unmeasured. Its own pre-commit guide flags git commit -am as a workflow limitation, while the available macOS history benchmark favors Kingfisher's runtime. [Release](https://github.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog/releases/tag/v3.97.9), [hook guide](https://github.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog/blob/e28360875917/PreCommit.md), [core tests](https://github.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog/actions/runs/36923757087).

layers.deciding_comparison: On the specified WSL2 Ubuntu x86_64 host, compare Kingfisher v2.9.1, Betterleaks v1.9.0, CredSweeper v1.18.5, TruffleHog v3.97.9 and Gitleaks v8.30.1 on the same held-out labeled corpus and seeded Git histories. Measure recall by credential family, false positives, historical secrets subsequently removed, merged and alternate refs, initial commits, partial staging and git commit -am. Record cold and warm pre-commit p50/p95 latency. Separate detection-only runs from provider-validation runs so network behavior and result filtering cannot obscure missed credentials. Measure each candidate's additional true positives beyond the leading scanner. The closest primary decision is Kingfisher versus Betterleaks; CredSweeper and TruffleHog could overturn it through better detection or distinct incremental coverage. Retain one scanner unless a second demonstrates a needed additional job.
evidence_gaps: The required ctx_fetch_and_index tool was denied with 'MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never.' Repository documentation and source were instead retrieved through the permitted GitHub API, indexed from those upstream bytes in /tmp with ctx_index, and read using ctx_search. This is a deviation from the requested page-fetch method.
Three web-search queries failed with an upstream timeout. The judgment uses verified repository sources and their cited evaluations; it does not claim an exhaustive search of public evaluations.

No comparison read here establishes current-release detection or false-positive superiority across the leading candidates on WSL2. Kingfisher's published comparison measures macOS history runtime and validation counts, not a labeled accuracy corpus or staged-hook latency.
The April 2022 CredData comparison combines training and test data. Its results are historical evidence, not a current benchmark for CredSweeper, Gitleaks or TruffleHog.

No target-host installation, WSL2 smoke test or agent-session enforcement test was performed. Linux x64 artifacts and CI, macOS arm64 artifacts and CI, and documented CLI/Git-hook integration support platform fit.

All nine repository APIs reported unarchived status and default-branch commits inside the 90-day window as of 2026-10-02. Gitleaks and Rusty Hog therefore were not excluded despite older releases. Issue-health evidence was limited to three recently updated issues per repository, rather than response-time statistics.
A second scanner's needed incremental job has not been demonstrated. Shared rule catalogs do not prove identical coverage, and detector counts do not establish recall.
Research budget used: 30 GitHub API requests, comprising 27 REST requests and three GraphQL requests; three attempted web-search queries; seven requested page fetches denied before completion.
